prediction.overall_explanation: No exploitable vulnerabilities were found that an untrusted external attacker can use to cause loss of funds, unauthorized access, or meaningful state corruption within the provided contract. All privileged state changes (adding/removing sources, setting wait, caging) are protected by the wards-based auth and additionally require the contract to be live. The only externally callable non-auth function, load(), can be called by anyone but only after cage() and only for sources previously lifted by an authorized account. While load() performs an external call to SourceLike(src).cure() before updating internal accounting (a pattern that could be reentrancy-sensitive), exploiting that would require a malicious/compromised source contract to already be present in srcs (i.e., introduced by an authorized party), which is out of scope per the threat model. The tell() gating logic prevents indefinite blocking because it allows retrieval after the wait period even if some sources were never successfully loaded.
